subject: RStan fails to install on debian testing

messages.author: 8d6e15be5b3dabd7
messages.subject: RStan fails to install on debian testing
parts:
Hello everyone,

I spend Sunday trying to install rstan following the instuctions listed on the page:
https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/Installing-RStan-on-Mac-or-Linux

and it failed to compile no rstan but its dependencies. Digging into the problem I found the solution.
The solution is simple: install not the lastest version of libssl-dev (1.1.0c-2),  but version 1.0 by the usual command

sudo apt-get install libssl1.0

The lastest version of libssl changed the definitions in its headers of some structures and the package PKI, needed by rstan, does not compile under libssl-1.1.0 but it compiles without a problem with libssl-1.0.

I hope that this information can reach other people trying to install rstan in debian testing or any system that install the latest version of libssl.

An advice in the page  https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/Installing-RStan-on-Mac-or-Linux  would certainly helps. 

All my best and thanks for accepting me in the group!!

Luciano

On Monday, December 12, 2016 at 6:19:19 AM UTC-5, Luciano Moffatt wrote:
The solution is simple: install not the lastest version of libssl-dev (1.1.0c-2),  but version 1.0 by the usual command

sudo apt-get install libssl1.0

The lastest version of libssl changed the definitions in its headers of some structures and the package PKI, needed by rstan, does not compile under libssl-1.1.0 but it compiles without a problem with libssl-1.0.

I'm glad that you found a solution. To clarify, PKI is needed by rsconnect, rsconnect is needed by shinystan, and shinystan is suggested by rstan. If anyone is in a situation where you cannot change the libssl version, then you probably could get rstan installed (with the BH, Rcpp, and RcppEigen packages) but not shinystan.

Ben
